title: Verbal Prefixes 1: The Concept (perfectivization plus a meaning shade)
titleRussian: Глагольные приставки 1: Концепция (вид плюс оттенок значения)
description: Russian builds new verbs by attaching prefixes to existing roots. The prefix typically perfectivizes the verb AND adds a meaning shade (across, until, out, completely, slightly, in). One root supports several prefixed verbs, each with its own meaning.
descriptionRussian: Русский язык создаёт новые глаголы, присоединяя приставки к корню. Приставка обычно делает глагол совершенного вида И добавляет смысловой оттенок («через», «до», «вне», «полностью», «слегка», «внутрь»). У одного корня бывает несколько приставочных глаголов, и у каждого своё значение.
intro: The motion book taught you prefixes on one narrow set of verbs. This one generalizes: prefixes attach to almost anything, and they do two jobs at once. They make a verb perfective, and they add a shade of meaning on top. That is why one English verb can correspond to five Russian ones. Which prefix a given verb takes for its plain perfective is not predictable and has to be learned per verb.
rules: A prefix attached to an imperfective verb usually creates a perfective verb. Читать → прочитать; писать → написать; делать → сделать.
A prefix typically adds a meaning shade. Прочитать = 'read through.' Перечитать = 'read again.' Дочитать = 'finish reading.' Same root, different shades.
A single English verb often maps to several prefixed Russian perfectives. The choice depends on the speaker's exact meaning.
The plain perfective prefix differs by verb: читать takes про-, писать takes на-, делать takes с-. Пере- and до- attach on top of the same roots for the 'redo' and 'finish' shades.
When reading, identify the root first, then the prefix; the prefix's typical meaning narrows the new verb's reading.
examples: Антон прочитал эту книгу за два дня. (Anton read this book through in two days.) Про- + читать → perfective, 'through to the end.'
Я перечитал письмо несколько раз. (I (m) reread the letter several times.) Пере- + читать → perfective, 'again, over.'
Маша дочитала статью к утру. (Masha finished reading the article by morning.) До- + читать → perfective, 'finish, reach the end.'
Я сделал всё домашнее задание. (I (m) did all my homework.) С- + делать → perfective, completion.
Лена переделала свой проект. (Lena redid her project.) Пере- + делать → perfective, 'redo.'
Антон написал длинное письмо. (Anton wrote a long letter.) На- + писать → perfective, completion.

tables.title: The six prefixes this track covers

items.prompt: Антон _____ эту книгу за два дня.
items.promptEnglish: Anton read this book through in two days.
items.hint: 'Read through to the end in a bounded time.' Which prefix tilts to 'through to the end'?
items.explanation: The bounded time 'за два дня' plus the meaning 'read it cover to cover' signals про- + читать → прочитал. Читал (impf) describes an ongoing process; перечитал means 'read again'; дочитал means 'finished a reading that was already in progress.' Only прочитал fits the read-through-to-the-end framing.

items.prompt: Я _____ письмо несколько раз, потому что не понял с первого раза.
items.promptEnglish: I (m) reread the letter several times because I didn't understand it the first time.
items.hint: 'Несколько раз' = repeated reading of the same letter. Which prefix tilts to 'again, over'?
items.explanation: 'Несколько раз' plus 'did not understand the first time' signals a repeated reading: пере- + читать → перечитал. The pf пере- form is the canonical 'reread.' Прочитал would be a single read-through; дочитал would be finishing an in-progress reading; написал would be a different lexical event entirely.

items.prompt: Маша _____ статью к утру и легла спать.
items.promptEnglish: Masha finished reading the article by morning and went to bed.
items.hint: She was already reading and reached the end. Which prefix marks 'finish what you started'?
items.explanation: The implied reading-in-progress plus the explicit 'reaching the end by morning' signals до- + читать → дочитала. The до- prefix marks 'finish what you have started.' Прочитала would frame the entire read-through (start and finish in one event); читала is the ongoing process; перечитала would mean she read the article again.

items.prompt: Лена _____ свой проект, потому что начальник нашёл ошибки.
items.promptEnglish: Lena redid her project because the boss found mistakes.
items.hint: Boss found mistakes → Lena did the project a second time. Which prefix?
items.explanation: The 'found mistakes' framing signals that Lena redid the project from scratch: пере- + делать → переделала. The pf пере- marks 'redo.' Сделала would be 'did it completely' (one-time completion, not a redo); доделала would be 'finished what was unfinished'; делала is the ongoing process.

items.promptEnglish: Anton wrote a long letter to his friend.
items.hint: One specific letter, completed. Standard pf of писать?
items.explanation: The standard perfective of писать takes the prefix на-: написать → написал. The completed-letter framing signals one-shot completion, not a rewrite. Писал is the ongoing process; переписал is 'rewrite, copy out'; дописал is 'finish writing something already in progress.'

items.prompt: Я _____ домашнее задание и сел смотреть фильм.
items.promptEnglish: I (m) did my homework and sat down to watch a film.
items.hint: Standard pf of делать; the homework is completed as a one-shot event.
items.explanation: The standard perfective of делать takes the prefix с-: сделать → сделал. The completed-homework framing signals one-shot completion. Делал is the ongoing process; переделал would mean 'redid'; доделал would mean 'finished homework that was already in progress' (also valid but less direct here).

items.promptEnglish: Lena read this book through to the end.
items.hint: The plain 'read it through' perfective uses which prefix?
items.explanation: Про- gives the plain read-through perfective: прочитала. Перечитала would mean 'reread'; дочитала 'finished off a reading already under way'; зачитала is a different, bookish verb.

items.prompt: Антон _____ упражнение, потому что в нём были ошибки.
items.promptEnglish: Anton redid the exercise because it had mistakes in it.
items.hint: Mistakes force a second attempt: which shade?
items.explanation: The redo shade is пере-: переделал. Доделал means 'finished off'; заделал means 'sealed up (a hole)'; разделал 'cut up'.

items.promptEnglish: Igor finished reading the article - one page had remained.
items.hint: Only the tail of the reading was left.
items.explanation: Finishing something already in progress takes до-: дочитал. Прочитал would frame the whole read-through; перечитал a reread; недочитал means he did NOT finish.

items.hint: 'Ещё раз' = again. Which prefix carries redo?
items.explanation: The redo shade is пере-: перечитала ('read again'). Прочитала is a first read-through, which 'ещё раз' contradicts; дочитала means finishing a read in progress.

items.promptEnglish: Lena finished writing the letter - only the last paragraph had remained.
items.hint: Completing a writing already under way.
items.explanation: До- marks carrying an unfinished action to its end: дописала. Написала would frame the whole letter as one act; переписала a rewrite; записала a quick note.

items.prompt: Лена _____ всё домашнее задание за час.
items.promptEnglish: Lena did all the homework in an hour.
items.hint: The plain one-shot completion of делать.
items.explanation: С- gives the plain perfective of делать: сделала. Переделала would mean she redid it; доделала that she finished a leftover part; the 'за час' frame fits one complete act.

blanks: Маша _____ всю книгу за выходные. (Masha read the whole book through over the weekend.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: The 'whole book in a bounded weekend' framing signals one complete read-through: про- + читать → прочитала (fem). Читала is the ongoing process (no bound); перечитала would mean 'read again' (no first-reading framing here); дочитала would imply a reading already in progress (the sentence does not set that up).

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон читал роман весь месяц и вчера наконец перечитал его до конца.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton read the novel all month and yesterday finally finished it.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Наконец ... до конца' (finally ... to the end) signals finishing something already in progress, so the prefix is до-: дочитал. Перечитал means 'reread', which wrongly implies a second pass; the context describes reaching the end of the first one.

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон долго писал письмо и наконец написал последний абзац.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton wrote the letter for a long time and finally finished the last paragraph.
errorCorrection.explanation: The letter was already in progress ('долго писал') and 'наконец' marks reaching its end, so the prefix is до- (finish what you started): дописал. Написал frames writing the whole thing as one fresh event, which double-counts the long writing already described. Переписал means 'rewrote', записал 'wrote down'. The до- prefix marks completion of an action already under way.

errorCorrection.sentence: В сочинении были ошибки, поэтому Антон написал его заново.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There were mistakes in the essay, so Anton rewrote it from scratch.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Были ошибки ... заново' (mistakes ... from scratch) signals doing the text a second time, so the prefix is пере- (redo): переписал. Написал means 'wrote (the first time)', which заново contradicts. Дописал would mean finished writing.

minimalPairs.context: Маша _____ свою работу, потому что в ней были ошибки.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha redid her work because there were mistakes in it.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Were mistakes' signals a redo from scratch: пере- + делать → переделала. Сделала would be 'did it completely' (one-time completion), which the mistakes-trigger contradicts (there must be a first attempt and a redo).

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each perfective by the shade its prefix adds to the root.

reviewVocab.definition: the plain perfectives of читать / писать / делать; read through, write, do (one-shot completion). The perfectivizing prefix differs: про- / на- / с-.
reviewVocab.example: Антон прочитал книгу, написал письмо и сделал задание.

reviewVocab.definition: the пере- perfectives: reread, rewrite, redo. Пере- adds the 'do it again' shade onto the same root.
reviewVocab.example: Лена перечитала статью и переделала отчёт.

reviewVocab.definition: the до- perfectives: finish reading, finish writing, finish doing something already in progress. До- adds the 'reach the end' shade.
reviewVocab.example: Маша дочитала книгу и дописала письмо к утру.
